change.describe: branch `pr-3` of discourse-graphite-3 against e25638dab0d4b98f99c8fe8976ccaae8f4fb9db3 (merge-base e25638d)
change.title: pr-3
change.description: Add BlockedEmail, to block signups based on email. Track stats of how many times each email address is blocked, and last time it was blocked. Move email validation out of User model and into EmailValidator. Signup form remembers which email addresses have failed and shows validation error on email field.
change.author: Neil Lalonde

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so changing the case of one letter gets past the block
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` compares strings exactly, and nothing normalises the value on either side. `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` exactly as typed (app/models/user.rb:87), and `BlockedEmail` stores whatever it was created with. So if `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, a signup with `Bad@Spammers.org` gets through. The domain blacklist next to it ignores case on purpose (`Regexp.new(..., true)`, spec/models/user_spec.rb:512-515), and `Invite` already normalises with `Email.downcase` (app/models/invite.rb:20). Suggested fix: run `Email.downcase` on the email before saving a `BlockedEmail` and before the lookup in `should_block?`, and add a spec with a mixed-case address.

findings.title: match_count is saved from inside User validation, so the statistics come out wrong
findings.body:
`should_block?` saves the counter while `User` is being validated, and the PR says the point of the counter is stats. Two things skew it:
1. `UsersController#create` validates twice: `user.valid?` at app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168 always runs, because it is the left operand of `&&`, and then `user.save` at line 172 validates again. For a `do_nothing` record both saves commit, so every signup counts twice.
2. In Rails 3.2 (Gemfile.lock:115), `save` runs validations inside its transaction and rolls it back when validation fails. For a `block` record, the increment made during `user.save` is rolled back. Only the one from the stray `valid?` survives.

So on signup a blocked address counts once only by accident, and any other path that changes a user's email and calls `save`/`create` never records a blocked match. Nothing tells the admin the numbers are wrong. Suggested fix: keep `should_block?` free of side effects, and record the match once, outside the `User` save transaction, in the code that handles the rejection (or with `update_column` after the transaction). Add a spec through `UsersController#create` that checks `match_count` changes by exactly 1.

findings.title: A server-rejected email is shown as "invalid" on the field
findings.body: Any server-side error on `email` adds the address to `rejectedEmails`: blocked, domain not allowed, or already taken (errors.email comes from `user.errors.to_hash`, app/controllers/users_controller.rb:198). The field then always shows `user.email.invalid`, the same text used for a malformed address. If the address is already registered, the user is told it is invalid rather than taken. Consider showing the server's message instead: keep a map from email to `result.errors.email.join(' ')` and use that as the `reason`.

findings.title: rejectedEmails is one array on the prototype, shared by every instance
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is evaluated once in `extend`, so every instance of `CreateAccountController` shares the same array. The controller is normally a singleton, so in practice the list just lasts for the whole page session. Still, the usual Ember pattern is to set it in `init` (`this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A())`). That avoids leaks between instances, for example in tests.

contracts.action: Signup failure response now includes `errors` and `values`, and the client remembers rejected emails
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing failure branch: flash the message and reset formSubmitted (create_account_controller.js:273,277)
contracts.before_after: Before, it flashed the error and re-enabled submit. Now it also pushes `result.values.email` into `rejectedEmails`, which (through the `rejectedEmails.@each` dependency) makes emailValidation fail and disables submit until the email changes. The server echoes the raw `params[:email]` (user.rb:87), so the pushed value matches `accountEmail`.
contracts.visible_effect: The email field shows the `user.email.invalid` text and the submit button stays disabled for that address.
contracts.failure_mode: If the ajax call rejects, the existing handler at line 282-285 flashes `create_account.failed` and nothing is pushed. A `StatementInvalid` or `NicknameUnavailable` response has no `errors` key, so nothing is pushed then either.

contracts.action: The User email validator now calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which writes match statistics
contracts.equivalent_path: Old User#email_validator (only the domain whitelist/blacklist, no side effects)
contracts.before_after: Validation used to be read-only. Now every validation where the email changed writes to blocked_emails. UsersController#create validates twice (valid? at line 168, then save at 172), and save wraps validation in a transaction that is rolled back on failure.
contracts.visible_effect: Signup with a blocked email fails with the `user.email.blocked` message; match_count and last_match_at are miscounted.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed save rolls back the stats update, so the counters are wrong without any error. Reported as a finding.

summary: This PR adds BlockedEmail with match statistics, moves email domain checks into EmailValidator, and has the signup form remember emails the server rejected. Two things to fix. First, the blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so changing the case of a letter gets past the block. Second, match_count is saved from inside User validation: UsersController#create validates twice, and Rails rolls the save transaction back when validation fails, so the counts come out wrong without any error. On the client, a rejected email always shows the generic "invalid" text, and rejectedEmails is one array shared on the prototype.
